claim_1.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of pre-vaccination PAXgene whole-blood RNA from elderly EM131 participants (age ≥65; training set n=91, test set n=47) showed that a 15-gene signature predicted response versus poor-response to HBV vaccination, with 62.2% accuracy in the test set for anti-HBsAg titres measured 1 month after the second Twinrix injection [absolute day not stated].

sources.quote: The accuracy of the resulting 15-gene signature was assessed on the EM131 training set by 10-fold cross-validation and on the EM131 test set and found to be 62.6% and 62.2%, respectively ( Fig. 4b,c , Supplementary Fig. 4 and Supplementary Table 4b ).
RNA was isolated from PAXgene blood samples according to the manufacturer's instructions.
The elderly data set was separated randomly into a training set composed of 2/3 (91 samples) of the samples and a test set composed of 1/3 (47 samples) of the samples ( Supplementary Table 1 ).
To identify pre-vaccination biomarkers of vaccine response, the data set was restricted to pre-vaccination samples (138/280 samples).
Though HBV titres were measured 1 month after the second dose, all patients were offered the third dose to conform to the approved regimen.

claim_2.claim: ELISA analysis of serum from 174 healthy adults showed that 37% mounted protective anti-HBsAg titres after two Twinrix injections [absolute day not stated], the lowest response rate among the vaccines tested.

sources.quote: The percentage of study participants that mounted protective Ab titres (anti-HBsAg: 10 mIU ml −1 , anti-Tetanus toxoid: 0.1 IU ml −1 , anti-Diphtheria toxoid: 0.1 IU ml −1 and anti-Cholera toxin: dilution 1:40) 16 17 18 were, in decreasing order, 95% for Tetanus, 84% for Diphtheria, 71% for Cholera and 37% for HBV ( Fig. 1b ).
Only the HBV vaccine involved an antigen to which all study participants were naive and presented the lowest response rate (37%, after two injections)
One-hundred and seventy-four generally healthy, HBV-naive, adult residents of Québec were divided into two groups to participate in this study.
Anti-hepatitis B surface antigen (anti-HBsAg) total antibodies were quantified in serum samples using the MONOLISA Anti-HBs PLUS kit (Bio-Rad catalogue number 72566).
